security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, fenced examples, and normal Proxmox template terms. SKILL.md and output.json contain documentation and marketplace content, not executable code or prompt injection. Operators should still review VM actions before applying them to production infrastructure.

remediation.issue: MCP examples use bash fences even though they are not shell scripts.
remediation.suggestion: Change fenced examples to text or tool-call prose to avoid implying shell execution.

remediation.issue: Destructive VM actions are listed without a confirmation note.
remediation.suggestion: Add a warning before delete or clone examples to confirm node, VM ID, and backup state.

content.value_statement: Manual VM template work can create slow deployments and inconsistent Proxmox images. This skill guides reusable templates for Cloud-Init, Kubernetes, and application workloads.
actual_capabilities: Plan base VM settings for Proxmox templates, including CPU, memory, disk, ISO, and bridge values.
Convert tested VMs into templates by setting the template flag.
Clone templates into named VM instances for application or Kubernetes nodes.
Describe Cloud-Init use for hostname, network, and post-clone configuration.
Recommend template versioning, hardening, testing, and cleanup practices.
limitations: Templates must be cloned before booting.
It does not import disk images or run Proxmox CLI commands directly.
Cloud-Init network settings still need validation on each target network.
Large templates can take longer to clone and move between storage pools.

use_cases.title: Build Kubernetes Node Templates
use_cases.description: Create RKE2-ready Ubuntu templates for repeatable control plane and worker node deployments.

use_cases.title: Standardize Server Provisioning
use_cases.description: Prepare web, database, or CI templates that clone into consistent production or lab servers.

use_cases.title: Maintain Template Versions
use_cases.description: Track patched, tested, and documented VM templates for infrastructure automation workflows.

prompt_templates.title: Create Basic Template
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a small Ubuntu template.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an Ubuntu 22.04 Cloud-Init template on pve2 with VM ID 100, 2 cores, 4 GB memory, and 50 GB disk.

prompt_templates.title: Convert Tested VM
prompt_templates.scenario: Turn a prepared VM into a reusable template.
prompt_templates.prompt: Mark VM 100 on pve2 as a template after I confirm packages, patches, SSH, and Cloud-Init are ready.

prompt_templates.title: Clone Cluster Nodes
prompt_templates.scenario: Deploy several VMs from one template.
prompt_templates.prompt: Clone template VM 100 on pve2 into three full clones for control plane nodes named rancher-1, rancher-2, and rancher-3.

prompt_templates.title: Refresh Template Lifecycle
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide a safe update of template VM 100 by creating a test clone, applying patches, validating services, and recording a new version.

output_examples.input: Create a basic Ubuntu template for shared services.
output: Plan: create a small Cloud-Init VM, install approved packages, apply patches, test a clone, then mark the source as a template.
Expected guidance includes CPU, memory, disk, network bridge, and Cloud-Init checks.
Safety note: remove credentials and temporary files before conversion.

output_examples.input: Clone a template for three Kubernetes control plane nodes.
output: The response names each clone, recommends full clone mode, and separates template preparation from cluster bootstrap.
After cloning, it directs hostname and network changes through Cloud-Init.
The final checks cover VM status, resource sizing, and cluster readiness tasks.
The response creates a temporary clone, applies patches, tests services, records a version, and replaces the old template after validation.
It also reminds the operator to document package versions and remove temporary data.

best_practices: Patch and harden the VM before marking it as a template.
Use Cloud-Init for hostname, network, SSH, and first boot configuration.
Document template names, versions, packages, and test results.
anti_patterns: Converting a VM that still contains credentials or temporary secrets.
Booting a template directly instead of cloning it first.
Using one large template for unrelated workloads with different security needs.

faq.question: Does this skill execute Proxmox changes by itself?
faq.answer: No. It provides instructions and MCP tool call plans for VM template workflows.

faq.question: Which environments does it target?
faq.answer: It targets Proxmox VE workflows using Cloud-Init, template conversion, cloning, and RKE2-oriented examples.

faq.question: Can it create Kubernetes templates?
faq.answer: Yes. It outlines an Ubuntu RKE2 template workflow and cloning plan for control plane and worker nodes.

faq.question: How should I handle credentials?
faq.answer: Remove credentials, tokens, host keys, and temporary secrets before converting a VM into a template.

faq.question: Can I use it with Terraform?
faq.answer: Yes. Use it to prepare and test templates, then let Terraform clone them at scale.

faq.question: What should I verify before publishing a template?
faq.answer: Boot a clone, test networking, confirm Cloud-Init behavior, and document package versions and patch dates.
